requirement: Interning through any clone makes the handle and its data available through every clone. A fresh cache has its own assignments.
rationale:
The tests cover both obligations of `requirements.sdk.validation-cache.shared_node_ids`.

**Interning through any clone makes the handle and its data available through every clone.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[clones_interning_the_same_data_concurrently_get_one_handle]` starts four clones of one `ValidationCache` and has each intern `Node(42)` concurrently.
  - It asserts that every clone gets the same handle.
  - It then asserts that the original cache's `node_data(ids[0])` returns `Node(42)`. The data was interned only through the clones, so this shows it is shared.
  - It asserts that a different value, `Node(43)`, gets a different handle, so sharing is not a degenerate constant.
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/contracts.rs#fn[saved_node_and_edge_inputs_survive_a_different_handle_allocation_order]` interns `Node(1)` through the original cache. It asserts that `first.clone().cache().intern_node(Node(1))` returns the same handle (`subject`). `Application` derives `Clone` and holds a `ValidationCache`, so this checks the clone-to-original direction.

**A fresh cache has its own assignments.**
- In the same test, `fresh` is built with `ValidationCache::new()`.
  - `fresh.cache().node_data(subject)` is asserted to be `None`, so the original's handle and data do not leak into the fresh cache.
  - `assert_ne!(fresh_target, target)` shows the same data gets a different handle in the fresh cache.
  - The test also checks that evidence loaded against the fresh cache resolves to the fresh handles.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept. The tests carry `{test}` references to the subject. There are no acknowledgments, and none are needed.
